properties.name: Lake Chad
properties.summary: Shallow endorheic lake shared with Chad, Niger, and Cameroon; open water has shrunk dramatically since the 1960s.
properties.description: Lake Chad once covered more than 25,000 km². Open water is now a fraction of that, replaced by marshes and receding shorelines. Nigeria's shoreline lies mainly in Borno and Yobe. The lake still supports fishing, recession agriculture, and transhumant pastoralism, and remains a focus of the Lake Chad Basin Commission.
properties.areaNote: ~1,350 km² open water (highly variable; far below 1960s extent)
properties.usage: Fishing, pastoralism, flood-recession farming, cross-border trade.
properties.ecology: Wetland birds, seasonal inundation, desertification pressure, invasive typha in some channels.
properties.climate: Sahel; rainfall decline and irrigation upstream affect inflows (Chari–Logone dominate).
properties.significance: UNESCO concern over shrinkage; security and livelihood hotspot of the basin.
properties.highlights: ["Shared by four countries","Severe 20th-century shrinkage","Livelihoods for millions in the basin"]

properties.name: Kainji Lake
properties.summary: Nigeria's largest man-made lake, impounded by Kainji Dam (1968).
properties.description: Kainji Dam was a flagship independent-era hydropower project. The lake drowned settlements and created a major fishery and Kainji Lake National Park on adjoining shores. Water level and generation vary with Niger River flow and plant maintenance cycles.
properties.maxDepthNote: ~12 m average; deeper near dam wall
properties.usage: Hydroelectric power, fishing, limited navigation, tourism (national park).
properties.ecology: Reservoir fishery; drawdown agriculture; wildlife in Kainji Lake National Park.
properties.significance: First large Nigerian hydro dam; anchor of Niger State's Power State identity.
properties.highlights: ["1968 Kainji Dam","Largest reservoir in Nigeria","National park shoreline"]

properties.name: Lagos Lagoon
properties.summary: Barrier-island lagoon behind Lagos; linked to the Atlantic through creeks and the harbour.
properties.description: The lagoon is the water body that made Lagos a port city. It receives Ogun and Osun drainage, urban wastewater, and sand-mining pressure. Water transport (Lagos Waterways) and fishing remain active despite pollution and siltation.
properties.maxDepthNote: ~2–5 m in main channels; shallower in flats
properties.usage: Fishing, sand mining, urban drainage, ferry transport, port access.
properties.ecology: Brackish water, mangroves (degraded), urban pollution hotspots.
properties.significance: Historic harbour of Eko; Lekki–Lagos urban waterfront.
properties.highlights: ["Made Lagos a port","Ferry network","Urban environmental pressure"]

properties.name: Oguta Lake
properties.summary: Imo State's largest natural lake; a tourism and fishing landmark in the southeast.
properties.description: Oguta Lake is a palm-fringed natural lake fed by the Njaba and Utu rivers. It hosts the Oguta Lake Holiday Complex, boat regattas, and lakeside settlements. Oil-palm processing and fishing sustain local communities.
properties.usage: Tourism, fishing, boat transport, cultural festivals.
properties.ecology: Freshwater fish species, riparian vegetation, linked wetland channels.
properties.significance: Major natural lake of the Niger Delta hinterland; Imo tourism icon.
properties.highlights: ["Oguta Lake Holiday Complex","Annual regatta","Two-river inflow (Njaba / Utu)"]

properties.name: Goronyo Reservoir
properties.summary: Large Sokoto basin reservoir supplying irrigation and downstream communities.
properties.description: Goronyo Dam impounds the Rima River to provide dry-season irrigation for the Sokoto–Rima basin and water for Sokoto city. Siltation and variable rainfall affect storage capacity.
properties.ecology: Seasonal drawdown exposes mudflats; bird habitat in wet season.
properties.significance: Key water-security asset for northwest Nigeria.
properties.highlights: ["Rima River impoundment","Sokoto irrigation scheme","Fishing livelihoods"]

properties.name: Dadin Kowa Reservoir
properties.summary: Gombe State reservoir on the Gongola, supporting hydropower and irrigation.
properties.description: Dadin Kowa Dam regulates the Gongola River for the Dadin Kowa hydro plant and downstream irrigation in the Upper Benue basin. The reservoir also supports fishing and livestock watering.
properties.significance: Major Gongola basin water infrastructure in the northeast.
properties.highlights: ["Gongola River regulation","Linked hydro plant","Upper Benue irrigation"]

properties.name: Asejire Reservoir
properties.summary: Oyo State reservoir on the Oshun River, supplying Ibadan and surrounding farms.
properties.description: Asejire Dam was built in the late 1960s to provide water for Ibadan and irrigation in the Oshun valley. The lake is a weekend recreation spot and supports a local fishery.
properties.usage: Domestic water for Ibadan, irrigation, fishing, recreation.
properties.significance: Primary water source for Nigeria's third-largest city.
properties.highlights: ["Oshun River impoundment","Ibadan water supply","Weekend recreation"]

properties.name: Challawa Gorge Reservoir
properties.summary: Kano basin reservoir feeding irrigation and the Challawa hydro plant.
properties.description: Challawa Gorge Dam impounds the Challawa River tributary of the Hadejia–Jama'are system. It supports Kano's hinterland irrigation schemes and the Challawa Gorge hydroelectric station.
properties.significance: Part of the Hadejia–Jama'are basin water infrastructure.
properties.highlights: ["Kano irrigation supply","Linked hydro plant","Hadejia system tributary"]

properties.name: Nigeria Coastline
properties.summary: About 853 km of Gulf of Guinea shoreline from the Badagry creek system to the Bakassi / Cross River estuary.
properties.description: The Nigerian coast is a mix of barrier islands (Lagos–Mahin), the Niger Delta mouths, and the eastern estuary around Calabar. It carries the bulk of seaborne trade, offshore oil, artisanal fisheries, and mangrove carbon stores. Coastal erosion, sea-level rise, and pollution are national planning issues.
properties.economy: Ports, offshore oil and gas, fisheries, coastal tourism, sand mining.
properties.ecology: Mangrove, barrier lagoon, turtles, and heavily pressured urban shores at Lagos.
properties.significance: Atlantic trade, oil terminals, fishing, mangrove ecosystems.
properties.highlights: ["Gulf of Guinea","Niger Delta outlets","Lagos barrier islands"]

properties.name: Lagos–Mahin Barrier Coast
properties.summary: Urbanised barrier-island coast from Badagry through Lagos to the Lekki peninsula and Mahin mud coast.
properties.description: Sand spits and barrier islands shelter Lagos Lagoon. The zone hosts Apapa and Lekki ports, dense urban waterfront, and chronic erosion. Ondo’s Mahin coast continues the barrier-lagoon pattern west of the delta.
properties.economy: Container ports, sand mining, real estate, fisheries, tourism.
properties.ecology: Lagoon, mangrove patches, urban pollution, turtle nesting (remaining beaches).
properties.environment: Erosion on Victoria Island and Lekki; wastewater and dredging.
properties.significance: National trade gateway; most populated coastal strip.
properties.highlights: ["Lagos Lagoon","Lekki Deep Sea Port","Badagry heritage coast"]

properties.name: Niger Delta Coast
properties.summary: Mangrove-fringed delta mouths from Ondo through Delta and Bayelsa to eastern Rivers.
properties.description: The Niger River and its distributaries create a low, tidal coast of creeks, mudflats, and mangrove. Oil terminals at Forcados, Escravos, and Bonny dominate export infrastructure; artisanal fishing sustains riverine communities.
properties.lengthNote: ~450 km of deltaic shoreline and creek mouths
properties.economy: Oil and gas export, fishing, palm produce, river transport.
properties.ecology: West Africa’s largest mangrove tract; high biodiversity; spill-sensitive.
properties.environment: Oil spills, gas flaring, mangrove loss, subsidence.
properties.significance: National oil wealth; blue-carbon and fisheries asset.
properties.highlights: ["Forcados & Escravos mouths","Bonny Island","Mangrove belt"]

properties.name: Cross River & Eastern Coast
properties.summary: Cross River estuary at Calabar through Akwa Ibom to the Bakassi / Cameroon border.
properties.description: Higher rainfall and clearer estuaries characterise the eastern coast. Calabar port serves the southeast; beaches at Ibeno and Bakassi mark the maritime frontier with Cameroon.
properties.economy: General cargo, regional export, fishing, emerging tourism.
properties.ecology: Estuarine mangrove, turtle beaches, lower oil impact than delta core.
properties.environment: Beach erosion; Bakassi transboundary wetland issues.
properties.significance: Eastern seaport; ICJ Bakassi boundary.
properties.highlights: ["Calabar estuary","Qua Iboe terminal area","Bakassi peninsula"]

properties.name: Apapa Port (Lagos)
properties.summary: Nigeria's busiest seaport complex; handles most national container traffic.
properties.description: Apapa and neighbouring Tin Can Island (TCIP) are the Lagos port cluster under the Nigerian Ports Authority, with private terminal operators. Congestion on the Apapa–Oshodi corridor has been a chronic logistics bottleneck. The ports remain the primary import gateway for the southwest and much of the north.
properties.economy: Containers, bulk, tank farms, trucking, bonded terminals.
properties.significance: National import hub, Apapa Wharf, Tin Can Island.
properties.highlights: ["Largest container throughput","Tin Can Island cluster","Lagos gateway"]

properties.name: Lekki Deep Sea Port
properties.summary: New deep-water port east of Lagos on the Lekki peninsula; 16 m draft container terminal.
properties.description: Lekki Deep Sea Port opened to relieve Lagos congestion with deeper draft and modern quay cranes. It sits within the Lekki Free Zone and connects to the Lekki–Epe expressway. Phase capacity targets multi-million TEU throughput.
properties.economy: Container trade, free zone, logistics parks, real estate.
properties.significance: First greenfield deep-sea port in a generation; Lekki Free Zone anchor.
properties.highlights: ["16 m draft","Lekki Free Zone","Relieves Apapa congestion"]

properties.name: Port Harcourt Port
properties.summary: Oil and general cargo port on the Bonny River up from the Atlantic.
properties.description: Port Harcourt's port (and nearby Onne) serve eastern Nigeria and the oil industry. Draft and dredging limit some vessel classes compared with Lagos; oil-service boats dominate. The city grew around this harbour from 1912.
properties.cargoNote: Oil export support, general cargo, project cargo
properties.economy: Oil export support, general cargo, eastern hinterland.
properties.significance: Garden City harbour, Onne satellite, eastern gateway.
properties.highlights: ["Bonny River port","Oil logistics","1912 foundation"]

properties.name: Calabar Port
properties.summary: Deep-water port on the Cross River estuary serving the southeast and Cameroon trade.
properties.description: Calabar has been a seaport since the Efik city-state era. The modern port handles general cargo and has been promoted for export processing. Silting and channel maintenance are recurring issues.
properties.cargoNote: General cargo, regional export, EPZ feedstock
properties.economy: General cargo, regional export, limited cruise/tourism.
properties.significance: Eastern seaport, historic Efik harbour.
properties.highlights: ["Cross River estuary","Historic port","EPZ hinterland"]

properties.name: Warri Port
properties.summary: Delta port for oil, steel, and agricultural hinterland cargoes.
properties.description: Warri Port on the Warri River serves the western delta industrial belt including the refinery and steel-related traffic. Access is via dredged delta channels toward Escravos.
properties.cargoNote: Oil products, general cargo, delta hinterland
properties.economy: Oil products, general cargo, delta logistics.
properties.significance: Escravos access, Warri industrial waterfront.
properties.highlights: ["Delta industrial port","Refinery city harbour"]

properties.name: Onne Port
properties.summary: Modern deep-water complex east of Port Harcourt; largest Nigerian port by land area.
properties.description: Onne (Federal Ocean Terminal / Federal Lighter Terminal and oil-and-gas free zone) was developed for energy logistics: rigs, pipes, and project cargo. It complements congested Lagos for specialised energy shipments.
properties.economy: Oil services, free zone, project cargo, containers (growing).
properties.significance: Energy logistics hub, free zone, large land take.
properties.highlights: ["Oil & gas free zone","Deep-water terminals","Largest port by area"]

properties.name: Lagos Lagoon & Barrier Coast
properties.summary: Shallow lagoon behind Lagos barrier islands; Atlantic access via Lekki and Lagos harbour creeks.
properties.description: The lagoon stretches from Badagry through metropolitan Lagos to the Lekki peninsula. It receives urban drainage from Lagos and Ogun, supports sand mining and fishing, and connects to the Atlantic through dredged channels. Victoria Island and Lekki sit on former barrier islands and reclaimed land.
properties.economy: Port access, sand mining, urban drainage, ferry transport, fisheries.
properties.ecology: Brackish water, degraded mangroves, urban pollution, siltation.
properties.environment: Coastal erosion on Victoria Island and Elegushi; wastewater and dredging pressure.
properties.significance: Historic harbour of Eko; Lekki Deep Sea Port gateway.
properties.highlights: ["Badagry–Lekki barrier chain","Lagos Waterways ferries","Lekki Deep Sea Port"]

properties.name: Niger Delta Estuary
properties.summary: Africa's largest delta empties through Forcados, Escravos, Bonny, and other distributaries into the Gulf of Guinea.
properties.description: The Niger River splits into a maze of creeks, mangrove channels, and sandbars across Delta, Bayelsa, and Rivers states. Oil terminals, artisanal fisheries, and riverine communities depend on these channels. Pollution and gas flaring have degraded parts of the delta wetlands.
properties.economy: Offshore oil, artisanal fishing, palm produce, river transport.
properties.ecology: Mangrove forest, turtles, seasonal floodplains, high biodiversity.
properties.environment: Oil spills, gas flaring, mangrove loss, subsidence in some areas.
properties.significance: National oil wealth centre; UNESCO Ramsar interest in parts of the delta.
properties.highlights: ["Forcados & Escravos mouths","Bonny Island channel","Mangrove carbon store"]

properties.name: Cross River Estuary
properties.summary: Tidal estuary at Calabar where the Cross River meets the Atlantic; eastern trade gateway.
properties.description: The Cross River estuary has served Efik and European trade since the 15th century. Calabar port sits on the estuary; silting and channel maintenance affect draft. The estuary links to Cameroon via historical trade routes and the Bakassi peninsula context.
properties.economy: General cargo, regional export, fishing, limited tourism.
properties.ecology: Mangrove fringe, estuarine fisheries, turtle nesting in nearby beaches.
properties.environment: Channel siltation; erosion on some eastern beaches.
properties.significance: Eastern seaport; historic Efik harbour; Cameroon border trade.
properties.highlights: ["Calabar port","Historic Efik city-state","Eastern EPZ hinterland"]

properties.name: Forcados Oil Terminal
properties.summary: Major Niger Delta crude loading terminal on the Forcados River mouth.
properties.description: Forcados terminal handles export crude from western delta fields via the Forcados pipeline system. Attacks and sabotage have periodically shut the terminal; dredged channels link to open sea tanker anchorage.
properties.economy: Crude oil export, tanker loading, oil-field logistics.
properties.environment: Oil spill risk; pipeline vandalism history.
properties.significance: Key western delta export hub.
properties.highlights: ["Forcados River mouth","Tanker anchorage","Western delta crude"]

properties.name: Bonny Oil Terminal
properties.summary: Bonny Island hosts Nigeria LNG and associated oil export infrastructure.
properties.description: Bonny Island in Rivers State is a major energy export node: NLNG trains, crude loading, and oil-service traffic. The Bonny River channel connects Port Harcourt and Onne to the Atlantic.
properties.economy: LNG export, crude oil, oil services, shipping.
properties.ecology: Island and mangrove interface; industrial footprint.
properties.significance: Nigeria LNG headquarters; eastern delta energy hub.
properties.highlights: ["NLNG trains","Bonny River channel","Island industrial complex"]

properties.name: Escravos Oil Terminal
properties.summary: Chevron-operated Escravos terminal exports crude and supports gas projects in the western delta.
properties.description: Escravos terminal on the Escravos River serves western delta oil and gas fields. Warri port and the Escravos–Warri road corridor link the terminal to the delta industrial belt.
properties.economy: Crude export, gas processing, delta logistics.
properties.ecology: Mangrove creeks; gas flare legacy in region.
properties.environment: Pollution pressure in western delta wetlands.
properties.significance: Major western delta export point; Warri industrial link.
properties.highlights: ["Escravos River","Warri corridor","Gas processing"]

properties.name: Lagos Coastal Erosion Belt
properties.summary: Victoria Island, Lekki, and Alpha Beach areas face chronic Atlantic erosion and storm surge.
properties.description: Sand mining, groynes, and sea-level rise interact along the Lagos open coast. Erosion threatens roads, estates, and beaches; Lagos State runs periodic beach nourishment and protection works.
properties.economy: Tourism, real estate, coastal engineering contracts.
properties.ecology: Intertidal zone loss; turtle nesting pressure on remaining beaches.
properties.environment: Sea-level rise, storm surge, sand mining, coastal squeeze.
properties.significance: Most urbanised erosion front in Nigeria.
properties.highlights: ["Victoria Island waterfront","Elegushi/Alpha Beach","Lekki peninsula"]

properties.name: Niger Delta Mangrove Belt
properties.summary: West Africa's largest mangrove tract — carbon store, fisheries nursery, and pollution-sensitive wetland.
properties.description: Rhizophora and Avicennia mangroves fringe delta creeks from Ondo through Bayelsa. Oil spills, deforestation for firewood, and land reclamation have reduced cover; restoration projects operate in parts of Rivers and Delta.
properties.ecology: Fish nursery, carbon sequestration, migratory birds, biodiversity hotspot.
properties.environment: Oil pollution, mangrove loss, gas flaring, climate vulnerability.
properties.significance: National blue-carbon asset; livelihood base for riverine communities.
properties.highlights: ["Rhizophora forests","Fisheries nursery","UN Ramsar sites nearby"]

properties.name: Bakassi Peninsula
properties.summary: Marshy peninsula at the Nigeria–Cameroon border; ICJ transfer to Cameroon (2008) with residual Nigerian communities.
properties.description: Bakassi sits on the Cross River estuary approach to the Atlantic. Fishing communities, border security, and mangrove wetlands define the area. The peninsula illustrates maritime boundary and livelihood issues on the eastern coast.
properties.economy: Artisanal fishing, cross-border trade, security patrols.
properties.significance: ICJ boundary case; eastern maritime frontier.
properties.highlights: ["Nigeria–Cameroon border","Cross River approach","Fishing communities"]

properties.name: Badagry Deep Sea Port
properties.type: Greenfield deepwater container and transshipment port
properties.summary: Largest single proposed Nigerian port project; a deepwater gateway at Badagry in Lagos State.
properties.description: Badagry Deep Sea Port is a greenfield facility promoted by the Badagry Port Development Limited (BPDL) consortium, hosted by 12 Badagry communities. Conceived in 2012 and repeatedly re-launched, it is pitched as one of Africa's largest deepwater ports and a West African transshipment hub, with a planned free-zone component.
properties.statusDetail: In September 2026 the Federal Government and APM Terminals (A.P. Moller-Maersk) signed a Memorandum of Understanding committing both parties to exclusive negotiations. Physical construction has not started.
properties.mouParties: Federal Government of Nigeria (Ministry of Marine and Blue Economy) and APM Terminals
properties.mouSignificance: The MoU commits the parties to exclusive negotiations on Badagry Port. It was signed by Vincent Clerc (Group CEO, A.P. Moller-Maersk) and Didi Ndiomu (Managing Director, Badagry Port Development Limited and Quinn McGrath Marine and Environmental Services).
properties.milestones: [{"date":"2012","event":"Concept conceived during the administration of Babatunde Fashola."},{"date":"2022-03-01","event":"Governor Sanwo-Olu announces a US$2.59bn Badagry seaport and free zone, with construction targeted for June 2022."},{"date":"2026-09-08","event":"Federal Government and APM Terminals sign MoU to develop the proposed Badagry Deep Seaport."}]
properties.capacity: Positioned to handle larger container vessels and cargo for West and Central African markets.
properties.significance: Intended West African transshipment and regional gateway.
properties.highlights: ["US$2.59bn planned cost","APM Terminals MoU (2026)","12 host communities"]

properties.name: Lekki Blue Sea Port
properties.type: Proposed deepwater port at the Lekki Free Trade Zone
properties.summary: A second, separate deepwater port proposed for the Lekki Free Trade Zone, distinct from the operational Lekki Deep Sea Port.
properties.description: Lekki Blue Sea Port is a distinct proposal from the operating Lekki Deep Sea Port at Itoke village. In October 2023 the Federal Ministry of Works signed a construction contract MoU with China Harbour Engineering Company Ltd for the project at the Lekki Free Trade Zone, alongside wider Nigeria-China infrastructure MoUs.
properties.statusDetail: Construction contract MoU signed in October 2023. No groundbreaking or physical works had been reported at the time of writing.
properties.mouParties: Federal Ministry of Works and China Harbour Engineering Company Ltd
properties.mouSignificance: Signed in Beijing at the 3rd Belt and Road Initiative Forum, witnessed by Vice President Kashim Shettima, as part of about US$2bn in Nigeria-China MoUs. The signing was led by Minister of Works Dave Umahi.
properties.milestones: [{"date":"2023-01-23","event":"The separate Lekki Deep Sea Port is inaugurated by President Buhari."},{"date":"2023-10-19","event":"Ministry of Works and China Harbour Engineering sign the Lekki Blue Sea Port MoU at the 3rd BRI Forum, Beijing."}]
properties.significance: Would add deepwater capacity alongside the operating Lekki port.
properties.highlights: ["BRI Forum MoU (2023)","Lekki Free Trade Zone","China Harbour Engineering"]

properties.name: Olokola Deep Sea Port
properties.type: Greenfield deepwater port and export processing zone
properties.summary: Ondo State's approved deep sea port project, originally paired with the Olokola Free Trade Zone.
properties.description: Olokola was first conceived with an accompanying Olokola Free Trade Zone and remained stalled for roughly two decades, with the original location failing to materialise from about 2004. Efforts were renewed from 2017 and the Federal Executive Council approved the establishment of a deep sea port in Ondo State in May 2023. Ogun State separately announced plans in November 2023 to sign a private-sector MoU for an Olokola seaport in Ogun Waterside, reflecting a long-running jurisdictional claim over the site.
properties.statusDetail: Approved by the Federal Executive Council in May 2023 after state and federal due diligence. Physical works have not started, and the site is claimed by both Ondo and Ogun State.
properties.mouSigned: Announced 30 November 2023 (Ogun State / Organised Private Sector); not confirmed as executed
properties.mouParties: Ogun State Government and the Organised Private Sector (stated intent)
properties.mouSignificance: Governor Dapo Abiodun said the state would soon sign an MoU with private-sector players on the Olokola seaport, alongside the planned Kajola dry port and Gateway Agro-Cargo International Airport.
properties.milestones: [{"date":"2004","event":"Original Olokola port/free-zone concept stalls."},{"date":"2017","event":"Renewed push under Governor Akeredolu, with due diligence by state and federal government."},{"date":"2023-05-17","event":"Federal Executive Council approves establishment of an Ondo State deep sea port."},{"date":"2023-11-30","event":"Ogun State announces intent to sign a private-sector MoU for Olokola."}]
properties.significance: Ondo's approved greenfield deepwater gateway.
properties.highlights: ["FEC approved 2023","Olokola Free Trade Zone","Ondo/Ogun site dispute"]

properties.name: Ibom Deep Sea Port (Akanassa)
properties.summary: Akwa Ibom's long-running PPP deep seaport at Akanassa in Mbo LGA; approved but repeatedly stalled.
properties.description: The project began as the Ibaka Deep Seaport before moving to Akanassa in Mbo LGA. It is a PPP sponsored by the Federal Ministry of Transportation, the Nigerian Ports Authority and the Akwa Ibom State Government, with PricewaterhouseCoopers and GMAPS as advisers. Construction stalled after host-community opposition to a possible relocation, prompting contractor withdrawals, and has since been under revival.
properties.statusDetail: The Outline Business Case was approved in 2015 and a phase-one tranche in December 2020, but construction has not begun. Following community opposition and contractor withdrawal, the Akwa Ibom government resumed engagement with China Harbour Engineering Company in 2022.
properties.mouParties: Federal Government, Akwa Ibom State Government and Nigerian Ports Authority (PPP); preferred bidder Bolloré Africa Logistics / PowerChina consortium
properties.mouSignificance: Bolloré Africa Logistics and PowerChina International were selected as preferred bidder with a 50-year operating franchise, with China Harbour Engineering Company as reserved bidder. A 50-year concession was approved in December 2016.
properties.milestones: [{"date":"2012-09","event":"Inception planning begins; project originally named Ibaka Deep Seaport."},{"date":"2015-05-13","event":"Federal Executive Council approves the Outline Business Case under a PPP model."},{"date":"2016-12","event":"A 50-year concession period is approved for investors."},{"date":"2018","event":"Bolloré–PowerChina consortium emerges as preferred bidder after an RFP process."},{"date":"2020-12-16","event":"FEC approves US$2.016bn for phase one."},{"date":"2022","event":"Renewed talks with China Harbour Engineering Company after earlier contractor withdrawal."}]
properties.significance: Southeast Nigeria's flagship approved greenfield deep sea port.
properties.highlights: ["FEC approval 2015","US$2.016bn phase one","50-year concession"]

properties.name: Bakassi Deep Sea Port
properties.type: Greenfield deepwater port and industrial park
properties.summary: A 16 m-draft deep sea port concept for the Bakassi peninsula, bundled with a large industrial park.
properties.description: Bakassi Deep Sea Port is a greenfield 16 m-draft port planned as the anchor of a 7,000-hectare Bakassi Industrial Park, intended to serve the North East as well as Chad and Niger Republic. Transaction advisers, including China Harbour, supported early structuring work under a project steering committee.
properties.statusDetail: A construction agreement for preliminary works was signed with China Harbour in November 2017, following project steering committee approvals in 2016. Physical construction has not commenced.
properties.mouParties: Cross River State Government and China Harbour Engineering Company
properties.mouSignificance: The agreement covered preliminary works for the Bakassi Deep Seaport and was described at the time as signalling commencement of the project. It is one of the five ports the NPA later listed as having completed federal approvals and compliance steps.
properties.milestones: [{"date":"2014-12","event":"Conceptual and technical studies completed."},{"date":"2016-02-08","event":"Project steering committee approval received."},{"date":"2016-05","event":"Project steering committee inaugurated."},{"date":"2017-11-23","event":"Cross River State signs preliminary works construction agreement with China Harbour."}]
properties.significance: Planned North East and Central African gateway via a 7,000 ha industrial park.
properties.highlights: ["16 m draft design","7,000 ha industrial park","Serves Chad and Niger"]

properties.name: Bonny Deep Seaport
properties.type: River-mouth deep sea port on a DBFOT concession
properties.summary: A relocated greenfield deep sea port on Bonny Island, pitched as a 500,000 TEU facility.
properties.description: Bonny Deep Seaport was first sited at Finima but relocated to Bonny Island after NNPC pipelines along the access channel blocked dredging at the original site. The new site has a natural draft of about 17 metres. The project is to be delivered by CCECC Nigeria Limited on a DBFOT basis and was flagged off by President Buhari in March 2022 alongside the Port Harcourt–Maiduguri rail line and a Railway Industrial Park.
properties.status: Flagged off · awaiting full federal approval
properties.statusDetail: Flagged off in March 2022 but reported as still lacking Federal Executive Council approval later that year. It was subsequently listed among the five approved deep seaport projects once approvals and compliance were completed.
properties.mouSigned: Flagged off March 2022; federal approval completed later
properties.mouParties: Federal Government and CCECC Nigeria Limited (DBFOT)
properties.mouSignificance: The March 2022 flag-off covered roughly US$3.2bn when the seaport was bundled with the Port Harcourt–Maiduguri rail line and the Railway Industrial Park.
properties.milestones: [{"date":"2021-09","event":"Minister of Transportation visits the Finima site to reconfirm location."},{"date":"2022-03","event":"President Buhari flags off the seaport, the rail line and the Railway Industrial Park."},{"date":"2022-09","event":"Site relocated from Finima to Bonny Island over NNPCL pipelines; still awaiting FEC approval."}]
properties.capacity: 500,000 TEU per annum; 100,000 DWT general cargo berth; 275.22 ha.
properties.significance: Planned eastern deepwater hub linked to the Port Harcourt–Maiduguri rail corridor.
properties.highlights: ["17 m natural draft","500,000 TEU/yr planned","CCECC DBFOT"]

properties.name: Agge Deep Sea Port
properties.summary: A US$3bn PPP deep seaport for southern Bayelsa that is active but still short of federal approval.
properties.description: Agge Deep Sea Port in Ekeremor LGA was formally announced in 2017, when Bayelsa acquired 15,000 hectares and inaugurated a 14-member implementation committee. Public reporting stalled between 2021 and 2023, then revived after the Federal Ministry of Marine and Blue Economy was created. Bayelsa has since established a dedicated state Ministry of Marine and Blue Economy.
properties.statusDetail: Not included in the batch of five ports the NPA reported as having completed federal approvals, because the Outline and Full Business Cases were incomplete, a transaction adviser was still being appointed, and evacuation corridors were unfinished. Concession terms were being restructured from 25 years to 40–45 years.
properties.mouSigned: Not signed to date; federal and state MoU discussions ongoing
properties.mouParties: Bayelsa State Government, Federal Government and a private investor (PPP)
properties.mouSignificance: A federal steering committee visited the site to accelerate approval. A joint steering committee is expected to coordinate the financial, technical and environmental workstreams needed for federal clearance.
properties.milestones: [{"date":"2017","event":"Bayelsa announces the project, acquires 15,000 ha and inaugurates an implementation committee."},{"date":"2021-2023","event":"Public progress stalls while background discussions continue."},{"date":"2023","event":"Interest revived under the new Federal Ministry of Marine and Blue Economy."},{"date":"2025-02","event":"Minister of Marine and Blue Economy leads a delegation to Bayelsa to accelerate the project."}]
properties.capacity: PPP scope reduced to about 7,000 ha; concession being restructured to 40–45 years.
properties.significance: Bayelsa's flagship maritime project and a designated blue-economy asset.
properties.highlights: ["US$3bn PPP","15,000 ha acquired 2017","Concession under restructure"]

properties.name: Ogidigben Deep Sea Port
properties.summary: An early-stage Delta State deep sea port concept reported alongside the national pipeline of planned ports.
properties.description: Ogidigben has been named in industry reporting as one of Nigeria's proposed deep sea ports, alongside the Lagos, Ondo, Akwa Ibom, Bayelsa, Cross River and Rivers projects. Unlike the Badagry, Ibom, Bakassi and Bonny projects it has not appeared in federal approval announcements, and no concession, contract or construction milestone has been publicly recorded.
properties.status: Conceptual · no recorded approval or MOU
properties.statusDetail: Named as a proposed deep sea port in industry reporting. No federal approval, MoU, transaction adviser or concession has been publicly announced for the site.
properties.mouSignificance: The project has not attracted a publicly announced MoU or partner, unlike the other Delta-area proposals.
